title: "Create a  Microsoft Foundry resource"
date: 2026-04-15
category: "Microsoft Foundry"
level: "Intermediate"
description: "Showing how to create a resource for Microsoft Foundry, previously Azure AI Foundry."
featureImage: "/images/categories/microsoft-foundry.png"
published: true
---

Before you startYou need an Azure subscription. If you don't have one, go to azure.microsoft.com/free and set one up — new accounts get a free credit for the first 30 days.Step 1: Create a resource group first
In the search bar, type Resource groups and open that page.Click + Create.Fill in:
Subscription: your subscriptionResource group: something like rg-foundry-learningRegion: pick one close to you, for example SWeden Central
Click Review + create, then Create.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Article image" style="width:100%" />
Step 2: Open the Azure portal and search for Foundry
Go to portal.azure.com and sign in.Click the search bar at the top of the page and type Microsoft Foundry.Under "Marketplace" in the results dropdown, look for the tile with publisher: Microsoft and type: Azure Service. Click it.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Article image" style="width:100%" />

You can also skip the search and paste this directly into your browser: portal.azure.com/#create/Microsoft.CognitiveServicesAIFoundry. It drops you straight onto the creation form for step 3.Step 3: Fill in the Foundry resource creation formBack on the Microsoft Foundry marketplace page  click Create. You land on a creation blade with tabs across the top: Basics, Storage, Inbound Networking, Outbound Networking, Identity, Encryption, Tags, and Review + create.On the Basics tab, fill in:Subscription: same one you used for the resource group.Resource group: select the one you just created.Region: match the region you picked for the resource group.Name: has to be globally unique across Azure, since it becomes part of your resource's endpoint URL. Something like foundry-yourname-learning. Letters, numbers, and hyphens only.Default project name: Microsoft folds "create your first project" into this same form. Type something like first-project for now.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Article image" style="width:100%" />
Leave the rest at their defaults for this first resource:Storage — a storage account gets created automatically if you leave this blank.Inbound Networking — defaults to public access (key or Entra ID authenticated).Outbound Networking — default is fine.Identity — default is fine.Encryption — Microsoft-managed keys by default.Tags — optional, skip for now.Foundry resources bill pay-as-you-go for what you actually use.Step 4: Review and create
Click Review + create.Wait for the green "Validation passed" banner.Click Create.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Article image" style="width:100%" />

Deployment takes one to two minutes. It's provisioning a resource of type Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts — the same underlying type Azure OpenAI and Azure AI multi-service resources use.When it finishes: "Your deployment is complete", with two buttons — Go to resource and Go to Foundry portal.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Article image" style="width:100%" />
Step 5: See what you got
Click Go to resource first. This opens the resource's Overview page in the regular Azure portal, where you'll find:
The resource's Endpoint URLKeys and Endpoint in the left-hand menu, where your API keys liveStandard Azure controls: Access control (IAM), Diagnostic settings, Cost analysis
Now click Go to Foundry portal instead. This takes you to ai.azure.com. In the upper-left corner you'll see the project name you typed in Step 3 (first-project) already selected, because creating the resource created that project too.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Article image" style="width:100%" />
That's it — you have a live Foundry resource with a project sitting inside it.Next: creating a project.
